newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli PM rejects unilateral Lebanon pullout.
newsitem.headline: Israeli PM rejects unilateral Lebanon pullout.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday rejected a unilateral Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, saying it would bring Hizbollah "terrorists" closer to Israel's northern frontier.

Netanyahu, speaking following Tuesday's mid-air collision of two Lebanon-bound Israeli helicopters that killed 73 soldiers, said Israel must stabilise its northern border before leaving its self-declared security zone.
"This border was at first grabbed by Palestinian terrorists and now it has been seized by Hizbollah terrorists who rely on Syria and Iran," he told Israel's Channel Two television.

"It is not easy to change this equation without at least changing the equation with Syria," Netanyahu said, alluding to the frozen Israel-Syrian peace talks and Damascus' role as a powerbroker in Lebanon.
"It is hard to think of any unilateral solution in which Hizbollah does not simply move nearer to the border after (Israel) leaves. That is the problem bothering me."
Netanyahu said he would have pulled Israeli troops out of Lebanon if he believed there was a "high probability" Hizbollah fighters would not deploy in the vacated areas.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Wednesday Israel should draw a lesson from Tuesday's crash and realise it was time to end its occupation of south Lebanon.

The debate over Israel's involvement in Lebanon had come up just before the crash when three soldiers were killed by a Hizbollah bomb. Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani complained the soldiers were sitting ducks.

But Israeli army chief of staff Amnon Shahak told Channel Two on Friday Israel would not leave: "Today I don't know of any other solution that appears better to me than what we are doing now -- with all the pain and the price entailed. There is a price to pay for security."

The 73 Israeli soldiers killed in the crash were three more than the fatalities inflicted by Hizbollah in the past three years on Israeli soldiers in Lebanon. The occupation zone was carved out in 1985 to prevent guerrilla attacks.
Hizbollah (Party of God), financed and armed by Iran, is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied local militia from Lebanon.
